A Note on Cabling and L-space surgeries

Jennifer Hom Address: Department of Mathematics, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA 19104
jenhom@math.upenn.edu
Abstract.

We prove that the (p,q)(p,q)-cable of a knot K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} admits a positive LL-space surgery if and only if KK admits a positive LL-space surgery and q/p≥2​g​(K)−1q/p\geq 2g(K)-1, where g⁡(K)g(K) is the Seifert genus of KK. The “if” direction is due to Hedden [2].

1. Introduction

In [6], Ozsváth and Szabó introduced a powerful tool for studying closed 33-manifolds, Heegaard Floer homology, and later equipped this invariant with a filtration (independently developed by Rasmussen in [11]) that defined an invariant for a knot in the 33-manifold. The relationship between the knot invariant and the Heegaard Floer homology of the 33-manifold obtained by Dehn surgery on that knot has been well studied (c.f. [8], [9], [10]), and can also be considered from the perspective of bordered Heegaard Floer homology [3].

In this note, we restrict our consideration to the simplest “hat” version of the theory, assuming that the reader is familiar with the finitely generated abelian groups

H​F^​(Y)andH​F​K^​(Y,K)\widehat{HF}(Y)\qquad\textup{and}\qquad\widehat{HFK}(Y,K)

associated with a 33-manifold YY and a null-homologous knot K⊂YK\subset Y (see [7]). We will write simply H​F​K^​(K)\widehat{HFK}(K) when it is clear that the ambient 33-manifold is S3S^{3}. For the present purposes, we do not need to concern ourselves with the gradings on these groups. We focus our attention on a class of 33-manifolds with particularly simple Heegaard Floer homology. For a rational homology sphere YY, we have that

rk​H​F^​(Y)≥|H1​(Y,ℤ)|.\mathrm{rk}\ \widehat{HF}(Y)\geq|H_{1}(Y,\mathbb{Z})|.

An LL-space is a rational homology sphere YY for which the above bound is sharp. The name comes from the fact that lens spaces are LL-spaces, which can be seen by examining the Heegaard Floer complex associated to a standard genus 11 Heegaard decomposition of a lens space.

We call a knot K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} an LL-space knot if there exists n∈ℤn\in\mathbb{Z}, n>0n>0, such that nn surgery on KK yields an LL-space. We will denote the resulting 33-manifold by Sn3​(K)S_{n}^{3}(K). Torus knots are a convenient source of LL-space knots, since p​q±1pq\pm 1 surgery on the (p,q)(p,q)-torus knot yields a lens space. It was proved in [8] that if a knot KK is an LL-space knot, then the knot Floer complex associated to KK has a particularly simple form that can be deduced from the Alexander polynomial of KK, ΔK​(t)\Delta_{K}(t). Thus, knowing that a knot KK admits a lens space (or LL-space) surgery yields a remarkable amount of information about the Heegaard Floer invariants associated to both the knot KK, and manifolds obtained by Dehn surgery on KK. In particular, results of [8] and [10] allow one to compute the Heegaard Floer invariants of any Dehn surgery on an LL-space knot KK from the Alexander polynomial of KK.

Recall that the (p,q)(p,q)-cable of a knot KK, denoted Kp,qK_{p,q}, is the satellite knot with pattern the (p,q)(p,q)-torus knot. More precisely, we can construct Kp,qK_{p,q} by equipping the boundary of a tubular neighborhood of KK with the (p,q)(p,q)-torus knot, where the knot traverses the longitudinal direction pp times and the meridional direction qq times. We will assume throughout that p>1p>1. (This assumption does not cause any loss of generality, since K−p,−q=−Kp,qK_{-p,-q}=-K_{p,q}, where −Kp,q-K_{p,q} denotes Kp,qK_{p,q} with the opposite orientation, and since K1,q=KK_{1,q}=K.) Let g⁡(K)g(K) denote the Seifert genus of KK. In Theorem 1.10 of [2], Hedden proves that if KK is an LL-space knot and q/p≥2​g​(K)−1q/p\geq 2g(K)-1, then Kp,qK_{p,q} is an LL-space knot. The goal of this note is to prove the converse:

Theorem.

The (p,q)(p,q)-cable of a knot K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} is an LL-space knot if and only if KK is an LL-space knot and q/p≥2​g​(K)−1q/p\geq 2g(K)-1.

We prove our theorem by methods similar to those used in [2]. An interesting question to consider is whether there are other satellite constructions that also yield LL-space knots.

Acknowledgements. I would like to thank Paul Melvin for his patience and encouragement, and Matt Hedden for helpful email correspondence.

2. Proof of Theorem

An LL-space YY can be thought of as rational homology sphere with the “smallest” possible Heegaard Floer invariants, i.e. rk​H​F^​(Y)=|H1​(Y,ℤ)|\mathrm{rk}\ \widehat{HF}(Y)=|H_{1}(Y,\mathbb{Z})|. In a similar spirit, an LL-space knot KK can be thought of as a knot with the “smallest” possible knot Floer invariants. For example, since

ΔK​(t)=∑m,s(−1)m​rk​H​F​K^m​(K,s)​ts,\Delta_{K}(t)=\sum_{m,s}(-1)^{m}\ \mathrm{rk}\ \widehat{HFK}_{m}(K,s)t^{s},

we see immediately that the total rank of H​F​K^​(K)\widehat{HFK}(K) is bounded below by the sum of the absolute value of the coefficients of the Alexander polynomial of KK, ΔK​(t)\Delta_{K}(t). A necessary, but not sufficient, condition for a knot KK to be an LL-space knot is for this bound to be sharp; see [8] for the complete statement. The spirit of our proof is that when either KK is not an LL-space knot, or q/p<2​g​(K)−1q/p<2g(K)-1, the knot Floer invariants of Kp,qK_{p,q} are not “small” enough for Kp,qK_{p,q} to be an LL-space knot. We will determine this by looking at the rank of H​F^​(Sp​q3​(Kp,q))\widehat{HF}(S_{pq}^{3}(K_{p,q})).

Recall that τ⁡(K)\tau(K) is the integer-valued concordance invariant defined by Ozsváth and Szabó in [4]. Let 𝒫\mathcal{P} denote the set of all knots KK for which g⁡(K)=τ⁡(K)g(K)=\tau(K). We begin by assembling the following collection of facts.

    where A^s​(K)\hat{A}_{s}(K) is the subcomplex of C​F​K∞​(K)CFK^{\infty}(K) defined in [10]. We may think of C​F​K∞​(K)CFK^{\infty}(K) as generated over ℤ⁡[U,U−1]\mathbb{Z}[U,U^{-1}] by H​F​K^​(K)\widehat{HFK}(K), in which case rk​A^s​(K)=rk​H​F​K^​(K)\mathrm{rk}\ \hat{A}_{s}(K)=\mathrm{rk}\ \widehat{HFK}(K) for all ss. rk​H​F^​(Sp​q3​(Kp,q))=p​q+sKp,q+tKp,qp​qandrk​H​F^​(Sq/p3​(K))=q+p​sK+tKq/p.\mathrm{rk}\ \widehat{HF}(S_{pq}^{3}(K_{p,q}))=pq+s_{K_{p,q}}+t_{K_{p,q}}^{pq}\qquad\textup{and}\qquad\mathrm{rk}\ \widehat{HF}(S_{q/p}^{3}(K))=q+ps_{K}+t_{K}^{q/p}.

p2​sK+(p−1)​tKq/p=0.p^{2}s_{K}+(p-1)t_{K}^{q/p}=0.

Therefore, since p>1p>1, we have that sKs_{K} and tKq/pt_{K}^{q/p} must both be zero, or equivalently, KK is an LL-space knot and q/p≥2​g​(K)−1q/p\geq 2g(K)-1. This completes the proof of the theorem.
